laws.name: California Paid Sick Leave Law
laws.description: California requires most employers to provide paid sick leave to employees. Employees accrue at least 1 day per 30 hours worked or receive 3 days upfront annually.

duration.notes: Minimum per year; or 1 day per 30 hours worked

other_requirements: Applies to all private employers regardless of size

laws.notes: Can be used for employee's own health condition, care for family members, or domestic violence/sexual assault related needs.

laws.name: California Family Care Leave
laws.description: California employees can use up to 5 unpaid days per year to care for a family member with serious health condition.

other_requirements: Worked at least 1,250 hours in past 12 months

laws.notes: Applies to employers with 5 or more employees. Complements FMLA protections.

laws.name: California Pregnancy Disability Leave
laws.description: California requires employers to provide up to 4 months of unpaid, job-protected leave for pregnancy-related disabilities.

other_requirements: Employee must be pregnant or have pregnancy-related condition

laws.notes: Applies to employers with 5 or more employees. Separate from FMLA.

laws.name: California Voting Leave
laws.description: California requires employers to provide 2 hours of paid time off for voting in any statewide election.

other_requirements: Not enough time outside work hours to vote

leave_types.notice_requirement: Notify employer before election day if possible

laws.notes: Applies to all employers. Time off should be taken before or after work when possible.
